subject: Urgent: Morning throughput/layer errors impacting HaloHealth - reports of cache thrash
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@halohealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@halohealth.com
Date: 2029-12-08T09:04:12-08:00
Subject: Severe morning spike - generation p99 up 6x, 5% error rate

Jonas / Redwood team,

We saw a major degradation during the 08:00-09:30 PST window this morning: p50 roughly normal, but p95/p99 spiked ~6x vs baseline and end-to-end errors rose to ~5%. Our app shows many 504s and token generation failures. Attached are a short log dump and a heatmap from our dashboard.

This started abruptly at ~08:12 while our scheduled daily batch (user-activity summarization) kicked off — curious if that aligns with any changes on your side. Please escalate — this is hitting active customers.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Reliability
HaloHealth

Attachments: halo-morning-spike-20291208.log, kv-heatmap-20291208.png

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@halohealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-08T09:18:40-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe morning spike - generation p99 up 6x, 5% error rate

Hi Sarah — received, and sorry for the impact. Looping in Marissa (SRE) and Ben (CS) for immediate triage. We're opening an internal incident and will send an actionable plan within 30 minutes.

Quick question: did you change any client-side batching or prefix routing rules in the last 72 hours? Any details about the daily job (concurrency/ttl) are helpful.

— Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, sarah.liu@halohealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-08T09:34:05-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe morning spike - generation p99 up 6x, 5% error rate

Thanks for the data, Sarah. Initial triage notes (high level):
- Symptom pattern (sharp p99 spike + increased 5xxs during a narrow time window) strongly suggests KV cache thrash / HOL blocking rather than model-level slowdown.
- Correlated with a batch job that appears to fan out a large number of cold prefixes into the serving path — this will inflate prefix cache misses and create head-of-line contention on certain hot lanes.
- I reviewed the log excerpt you attached: many repeated cache miss/error pairs and request queue depth spikes on a small subset of hosts.

Immediate mitigations we propose (can apply as hotfixes):
1) Temporarily reduce the per-batch concurrency for the scheduled job (recommended drop to 25% of current) so we stop creating mass cold-prefetch pressure.
2) Enable conservative KV TTL bump for HaloHealth tenant keys (+30s) to reduce churn for rolling windows.
3) Switch affected routes to a lower-aggregation lane that avoids shared hot partitions (will cost some throughput but improves p99).
4) If spike continues, we can enable a short-term global prefix-probing backoff and increase KV cache capacity for the tenant pool.

I'm attaching a short mitigation playbook (mitigation-playbook-v1.md) and a heatmap save for our reference. Ben — please coordinate the change window with Halo. Rishi — please prep a fast rollback if any of these hotfixes affect throughput negatively.

Marissa Cole
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-playbook-v1.md

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@halohealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-08T10:02:11-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe morning spike - generation p99 up 6x, 5% error rate

Thanks Marissa — we can throttle the batch job immediately (we control the schedule). Two asks before you push:
- ETA on when TTL bump and lane switch would be in effect? We need to minimize customer impact.
- Can you confirm there's no config change needed on our side other than throttling the job?

Ben — can you please advise on the customer comms cadence; our leadership will want an interim update in the next hour.

Michael Torres
Production Engineer, HaloHealth

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: michael.torres@halohealth.com, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-08T10:18:40-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe morning spike - generation p99 up 6x, 5% error rate

Mike — I'll send HaloHealth leadership a one-line interim note now: "We have identified cache churn from a morning batch as the likely root cause; Redwood is implementing priority mitigations (batch throttle + cache TTL lift + route isolation) and will confirm impact in 30 minutes."

We'll follow up with the technical summary and next steps once Marissa's changes are applied. Please confirm when you've throttled the job.

— Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, sarah.liu@halohealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-12-08T16:42:05-08:00
Subject: Incident update & closure: KV-churn mitigation applied (SUP-8721)

Update (post-mitigation):
- Timeline: 09:30 applied batch throttle (Halo), 09:42 applied tenant TTL bump and route isolation. Observed p99 drop from 6x -> ~1.3x within three consecutive windows and 5xxs returned to baseline by 10:05.
- Root cause: sudden burst of cold-prefix population from customer-side daily batch combined with a lower-than-expected tenant cache partitioning factor. This exposed hot-lane HOL blocking and thrash under write-heavy prefetch.
- Actions taken: temporary batch concurrency reduction, +30s tenant TTL, route isolation to lower contention lanes, enabled targeted prefetch backoff.
- Follow-ups (action items):
  * Rishi to propose a permanent tenant partitioning change and an automated prefetch-controller by 2029-12-15 (JIRA SUP-8721).
  * Jonas/Ben to coordinate a short RCA note for Halo leadership and offer a runbook for safe batch sizing.
  * Ops run (Marissa + Rishi) to run chaos-style tests on the batch pipeline in staging next week.

I'll keep the ticket open until Rishi's design is in review, but the service is back to normal and we've restored the SLA metrics to target. If you want a 1:1 technical review this afternoon, I have a 3pm slot.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-playbook-v1.md, halo-morning-spike-20291208.log
